thread:
Aisha Khan: @here PagerDuty just opened a PAGER for cont-batch p99 on streaming path in us-west-2. p99 jumped ~4x over the last 6m, customers with streaming sessions are observing stalls. Investigating now.

IncidentBot: INCIDENT created (sev: P2) — contbatch_streaming_tail_latency — triggered by alert: contbatch.streaming.p99 > 1200ms (5m).

Ben Ko: oncall here — grabbing logs. any obvious rollout?

Carmen Li: no deploys in the last hour according to deploy-bot. I see a lot of mixed seq lengths on the queues, and a small cluster of GPUs with KV eviction thrash.

Samir Patel: throwing up the quick query:
```
SELECT queue_id, avg(seq_len) as avg_len, p99_latency
FROM contbatch.metrics
WHERE region='us-west-2' AND timeframe='5m'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY p99_latency DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

Samir Patel: results show queue 42 and 43 with avg_len 850 and 1200 and p99 of 1800ms and 2300ms respectively. Most other queues are fine.

Jules Park: that matches KV churn on nodes gpu-uw2-0{7,8}. I'm seeing heavier-than-normal prefix hits causing padding amplification. Could be the mixed sequences causing big batches to stall waiting for long requests.

Ben Ko: can we pin the streaming route to a smaller max_batch_size as a quick mitigation? current config: max_batch_size=64, target_latency=200ms. Suggestation: set max_batch_size=12 for streaming queues 42/43.

Carmen Li: +1. smaller batches for streaming reduces tail amplification. Also enable preemptive scheduling (fair_share_preempt=true) for those workers.

Aisha Khan: do it and report back. If we need to, we'll open a fallback route to the quantized model (latency slightly higher for small responses but more consistent).

Ben Ko: making the change now:
```
# patch applied via ops-config
routes.streamers.42.max_batch_size = 12
routes.streamers.43.max_batch_size = 12
routes.streamers.42.scheduling.preemptive = true
routes.streamers.43.scheduling.preemptive = true
```

Ben Ko: pushed, reloading batcher on nodes (rolling restart) — 6 nodes at a time.

PagerDuty: Acknowledged by Ben Ko.

Carmen Li: I'm starting to see p99 drop on queue 42 from 1800ms -> 450ms after the change. queue 43 still at ~900ms but trending down. good signal.

Samir Patel: adding a temporary hedging policy for long tails: if a request hasn't started generating tokens in 350ms, spawn a hedged smaller-batch worker. This should reduce stalls for heavy seqs.

Aisha Khan: Good. @Carmen can you also check KV cache hit rates? If those are low we may need to reduce live page size or bump KV capacity on the affected nodes.

Carmen Li: KV hit rate for those nodes dropped from 92% -> 67% during surge. There's a KV churn pattern correlated with the long sequences. I'm going to evict cold keys more aggressively and extend the cache TTL for recent prefixes.

Jules Park: FYI I see a spike in large-ticket API traffic from one customer (acct: harmony-analytics) sending very long context windows repeatedly. Could be a single tenant causing mixed-seq amplification.

Aisha Khan: @Ben can you spin up an isolation route for that tenant to cap their concurrency or route them to Dedicated if they need sustained long contexts? We want to avoid noisy-neighbor impact.

Ben Ko: Created tenant route:
```
tenants.harmony-analytics.concurrency_limit = 4
tenants.harmony-analytics.route = fallback-small-quant
```
Pushing now.

Ben Ko: pushed, and OPS: throttled per-tenant concurrency is applied. early telemetry shows their requests falling to 3 concurrent streams.

Carmen Li: p99 across streaming now down to ~320ms cluster-wide. queue 43 at 420ms. still above target but within acceptable SLO window.

Samir Patel: I'll schedule a non-urgent postmortem to dig into why mixed seqs + our batching heuristics amplified tail. Hypothesis: our batch-assembly timeout + greedy packer waits for long seqs, causing short seqs to pack behind them during certain traffic patterns.

Aisha Khan: Action items (quick):
- short: reduce max_batch_size for affected streaming queues (Ben) — DONE
- short: enable preemptive scheduling and hedging (Ben/Samir) — DONE/IN-PROGRESS
- short: cap tenant concurrency and route to fallback (Ben) — DONE
- short: KV cache tweaks (Carmen) — IN-PROGRESS
- medium: collect traces for 1h and onboard to trace-dashboard; trigger postmortem (Samir) — TODO
- medium: run synthetic mixed-seq load test against batcher packer and measure tail amplification (Jules/Samir) — TODO

Jules Park: also recommend tuning packer thresholds: reduce pack_wait_ms for streaming to 6ms (was 18ms) to avoid prolonged waiting for alignment. That plus smaller max_batch_size should cut packing-induced latency.

Ben Ko: applying pack_wait_ms change on the streaming pool now.

Carmen Li: Customer impact assessment: currently 17 active streaming sessions reported errors/timeouts during the 10m peak. No confirmed loss of data. Customer support pinged for impacted tenants: harmony-analytics and two small customers. I've started DM thread with CSM.

Aisha Khan: If customers ask we should state root cause is transient scheduling and KV churn causing batching amplification; mitigation actions are applied and we're doing a deeper review. Keep comms conservative.

Samir Patel: logging note: capture full packet of a stalled request (include seq_len, header flags, route decisions) into staging S3 bucket for analysis. Will redact PII.

Ben Ko: p99 at the node group level is now stable ~310ms for last 5m. Will keep monitoring for 30m.

IncidentBot: INCIDENT update: mitigations applied; severity downgraded to P3.

Aisha Khan: Great work team. We'll leave this thread open for postmortem notes. If p99 creeps back up, re-escalate. :thumbsup:

Jules Park: I'll start the packer unit test matrix to reproduce mixed-seq amplification tomorrow.

Carmen Li: tagging folks for PM follow-up: @product-infra for KV sizing, @runtime for packer heuristics.

Ben Ko: monitoring alarms adjusted: added temporary rule to alert if contbatch.streaming.p99 > 800ms for >3m while the packer tuning is in flux.

Samir Patel: I'll own the postmortem and will follow up with timeline and action items in #postmortems.

Aisha Khan: Closing note: no customer escalations pending; keep eyes open.

PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by Aisha Khan, Ben Ko.
